title: Unpaid Education Overpayments Held Back From Post-9/11 Entitlement on an Election
content:
**Debt liaison guidance — Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education) elections, read with the student's Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery records.**

**Rule.** Days held back for an unpaid overpayment follow the student's education debt — the debt on the student's Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery records that arose from education benefits:
- when the education debt is being collected, in a repayment plan or active, with a balance above nothing, the current balance is held back;
- when the education debt is on hold for a pending request, the original amount is held back;
- otherwise nothing is held back.

An amount held back is turned into days over a 30-day month at the student's paid monthly rate — the amount multiplied by 30 and divided by the monthly rate it converts at — and those days are taken off the Post-9/11 entitlement credited on the election.

| Education debt status | Balance | Amount held back |
|---|---|---|
| Repayment plan | Above nothing | Current balance |
| Active | Above nothing | Current balance |
| Repayment plan or active | Nothing | Nothing |
| On hold for a pending request (waiver, dispute or compromise) | Any | Original amount |
| Paid in full, waived, compromised or referred to the Treasury | Any | Nothing |
| No education debt on file | — | Nothing |

**Hypothetical cases.** An education debt in a repayment plan with an original amount of $3000.00 and a current balance of $1259.00: $1259.00 is held back. The same debt on hold while a waiver request is pending: $3000.00 is held back. The same debt paid in full: nothing is held back.
